paper_title: PELMS Pre-training for Effective Low-Shot Multi-Document Summarization
caption: Low-shot pre-trained model performance on the multi-document summarization (MDS) task with ROUGE-G scores (geometric mean of ROUGE-1/2/L) aggregated over 6 MDS benchmarks. We compare with fully-supervised training (solid lines) and with adapter training (dashed lines) where only 5% of model parameters are tuned. achieves stronger overall performance at all data quantities and training methods when compared to competitive long-input summarization models.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of several models on the multi-document summarization (MDS) task, measured by the overall ROUGE-G score (geometric mean of ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L), as a function of the number of training examples, ranging from 0 to 64 on a linear scale. The y-axis represents the Overall ROUGE-G Score, also on a linear scale, ranging from 11.0 to 19.0. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model and training method: PELMS (solid green line with circular markers), PELMS (5%) (dashed green line with circular markers), Primera (solid red line with square markers), Primera (5%) (dashed red line with square markers), Pegasus-X (solid blue line with triangular markers), and Pegasus-X (5%) (dashed blue line with triangular markers). The Centrum model is represented by a solid yellow line with diamond markers, and Centrum (5%) by a dashed yellow line with diamond markers. At 0 training examples, PELMS achieves a score of approximately 17.0, while PELMS (5%) starts at about 17.0 as well; Primera begins at around 15.0, and Pegasus-X starts at approximately 13.0. As the number of training examples increases to 16, PELMS rises to about 18.0, PELMS (5%) to 17.5, Primera to 16.5, and Pegasus-X to 15.0. At 64 training examples, PELMS reaches approximately 18.5, PELMS (5%) reaches 18.0, Primera reaches 18.0, and Pegasus-X reaches 17.0. The Centrum model remains relatively flat, scoring around 15.0 at 0 examples and 15.5 at 64 examples, with its 5% variant showing a slight increase from 15.0 to 15.5. The dashed lines for all models indicate adapter training with only 5% of parameters tuned, while solid lines represent fully-supervised training. PELMS consistently outperforms the other models across all training example counts and methods.
